drivers.label: Novelty
drivers.text: Remotely heating supermarket fridges is a new kind of attack.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Hundreds of stores across several chains were affected.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Researchers found thousands of these controllers exposed online.

story.happened: Attackers remotely forced defrost cycles at refrigeration systems in French supermarkets from October 11, Infosecurity Magazine reports. Intermarché said 150 stores were hit and Carrefour 80. Danfoss said affected units ran obsolete or un-updated controllers. Belgium and the Netherlands were reportedly affected.

meme.bottom: The internet turned up the heat
meme.take: Lesson from France: a fridge does not need Wi-Fi to stay cool. It needs the opposite.

story.next: Watch for findings from France's cybersecurity agency and whether attackers are identified.
story.summary: Intermarché, Carrefour, Super U and Monoprix stores were hit through outdated Danfoss refrigeration controllers.
story.title: Hackers heat supermarket fridges across France, spoiling food
story.why: It is a rare attack where hacking caused direct physical damage in everyday shops.

story.background: GitLab is a widely used platform for storing code and running software builds.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: 10.0 is the highest severity score on the CVSS scale.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Self-managed releases going back to 2014 are affected, per the report.

story.happened: GitLab released emergency patches for an integer overflow in its bundled Onigmo regex library, The Hacker News reports. It allows code execution without logging in on self-managed servers since version 7.0. GitLab says it knows of no active attacks.

meme.bottom: On the one scale nobody wants
meme.take: GitLab finally got a perfect 10, on the severity scale.

story.next: Watch for whether attackers begin targeting unpatched servers.
story.summary: The bug, rated CVSS 10.0, lets attackers run code without logging in and affects releases back to 2014.
story.title: GitLab patches a maximum-severity flaw in self-managed servers
story.why: Many companies host their own GitLab, which holds source code and deployment secrets.

story.background: GlobalFoundries is a US contract chipmaker that builds chips designed by other companies.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Up to $21 billion of funding comes from Japan.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Each site would add 900,000 wafers a year.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Governments are paying to bring chipmaking home.

story.happened: GlobalFoundries will build and operate two 300mm fabs at its Malta, New York campus with up to $21 billion of Japanese funding, a company release says. The US Commerce Department takes about a 4% stake. The first fab is slated for 2029 after a late-2026 groundbreaking.

meme.bottom: Funded by Japan, part-owned by the US
meme.take: The future of American chipmaking is a group project, which is how the best ones go.

story.next: Watch for the groundbreaking later in 2026 and details of the US stake.
story.summary: Up to $21 billion in Japanese money will build two 300mm fabs at Malta, New York, with the US taking a small stake.
story.title: GlobalFoundries will run two new New York chip plants funded by Japan
story.why: It is a large bet on making more chips in the US under a US-Japan deal.

story.background: Google Cloud rents computing power to businesses. Revolut is a UK-based digital bank.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Several banks rely on the same cloud region.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Outages show how much banking depends on a few cloud providers.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Revolut has tens of millions of customers.

story.happened: The outage began late Monday Pacific time in Google's London region, Bloomberg reports, and Google blamed a power event. Revolut's app, card payments, transfers and ATM withdrawals were disrupted for hours. Revolut said money and data were safe.

meme.bottom: UK banking apps had a quiet night
meme.take: A single power problem in London reminded UK banks exactly whose computer they live on.
meme.top: Google Cloud had a power event

story.next: Watch for Google's full incident report and any response from UK regulators.
story.summary: A 'power event' in Google's London region took down banking apps for hours, with Revolut listing 31 services affected.
story.title: Google Cloud outage in London knocks out Revolut and other UK banks
story.why: When one cloud region fails, millions of people can lose access to their money at once.

story.background: Australia's under-16 social media ban, in force since December 2025, was the first of its kind.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Australia, Denmark and others have moved on similar age limits.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: Platforms have about ten weeks to build age checks.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Age checks could reach every Greek social media user.

story.happened: Platforms may use Greece's Kids Wallet or Gov.gr Wallet for age checks, but other reliable methods are allowed, Greek Reporter says. Children born in 2012 count as 15 from January 2027. PM Kyriakos Mitsotakis said firms have about two and a half months to prepare.

meme.bottom: The algorithm has ten weeks to grow up
meme.take: Greek teens born in 2012 qualify on January 1. Everyone else gets a very long wait for an app.
meme.top: Greece set a social media age limit

story.next: Watch for which age-check methods the big platforms choose before January.
story.summary: Parliament approved the law early on October 23. It starts on January 1, 2027, and platforms must check users' ages.
story.title: Greece passes a social media ban for children under 15
story.why: Countries are increasingly setting age limits for social media, and enforcement falls on the platforms.

story.background: Intel is a US chipmaker. Quantum computers use quantum physics to tackle some problems ordinary computers cannot.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: About $2.2 billion for a 130-person software company.

drivers.label: First of its kind
drivers.text: It is Intel's first major deal in four years.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Big tech firms are betting on quantum computing.

story.happened: Globes and Calcalist put the price at about $2.2 billion to $2.3 billion. Classiq has raised over $200 million and employs about 130 people. Closing is targeted for the first half of 2027.

meme.take: Intel is buying quantum software for $2.2 billion. The hardware remains in a superposition.

story.next: Watch for official confirmation from Intel and regulators' review.
story.summary: Intel agreed to buy Tel Aviv-based Classiq, its first major acquisition in four years, Israeli media report.
story.title: Intel is reported to buy quantum software firm Classiq for about $2.2 billion
story.why: It marks a new push into quantum computing by a chipmaker trying to rebuild its position.

story.background: Intel is one of the oldest chipmakers and makes processors for PCs and servers.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: A weak forecast overshadowed a beat.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Shares fell as much as about 20% after hours.

story.happened: Intel forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, below what analysts expected, Shacknews reports. Shares closed at $92.07 and fell as low as $73.50 after hours.

meme.take: Intel had a good quarter and a forecast that ended it.

story.next: Watch for how shares trade on Friday and what Intel says about demand.
story.summary: Intel's third-quarter revenue of $16.5 billion and EPS of $0.52 beat forecasts, but its fourth-quarter outlook disappointed.
story.title: Intel beats estimates but its forecast sends shares lower
story.why: Intel's turnaround is closely watched, and guidance matters more than a single beat.

story.background: Siri is Apple's voice assistant, first launched on the iPhone 4S in 2011.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: Apple is racing to catch up with Google and OpenAI assistants.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: It reaches recent iPhones worldwide.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: It fixes over 160 security flaws.

story.happened: Siri AI now recalls past conversations and reads more app context, and needs an iPhone 15 Pro or later, MacRumors reports. It still is not available in the EU or mainland China. The update fixes over 160 vulnerabilities.

meme.bottom: And you can tell it what to forget
meme.take: Siri now remembers past conversations. Apple added a setting for things it should not.
meme.top: Siri can now remember your chats

story.next: Watch for when Siri AI reaches the EU and China.
story.summary: Apple's iOS 27.2 adds Siri memory of past chats, an Excluded Apps setting, five new Siri languages and over 160 security fixes.
story.title: iOS 27.2 gives Siri conversation memory and a way to block apps from it
story.why: It is the biggest step yet for Apple's revamped Siri, which has trailed rival assistants.

story.background: The iPad mini is Apple's smallest tablet, first released in 2012.

drivers.label: First of its kind
drivers.text: It is the first iPad mini with an OLED screen.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: The starting price has risen $200 since the previous model launched.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: It opens Apple's run of launches this week.

story.happened: The iPad mini starts at $699, TechRadar reports, up from $499 at the last model's launch. It has 1,200-nit peak brightness, Apple's C2 modem in cellular models and is 5.33mm thin. Orders open October 28 and it ships November 6.

meme.bottom: The price got a promotion too
meme.take: Apple's iPad mini is thinner, brighter and $200 pricier than before. Only one thing grew.
meme.top: The iPad mini got an OLED screen

story.next: Watch for reviews and how buyers react to the price.
story.summary: The eighth-generation iPad mini gets an 8.5-inch OLED screen, IP67 water resistance and a thinner, lighter body.
story.title: Apple unveils an OLED iPad mini with A20 Pro chip from $699
story.why: It is the mini's biggest redesign in years, but the higher starting price has drawn attention.

story.background: Folding phones use flexible inner screens, and the crease at the hinge has long been their weak point.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: An inner screen repair costs $999 without AppleCare+.

drivers.label: Controversy
drivers.text: Coverage has already dubbed it Crackgate, with a question mark.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Reviewers' fold tests over thousands of cycles found wear but no cracks.

story.happened: GSMArena reports more buyers describing inner display damage linked to a possible hinge defect. MacRumors says pre-order shipping estimates slipped to January 2027. Apple has not commented on the cracks.

meme.bottom: A few say it went further
meme.take: Apple's first foldable has early crack reports. Folding was meant to be the hard part.
meme.top: The iPhone Duo folds in half

story.next: Watch for any statement from Apple or a repair programme.
story.summary: More early iPhone Duo buyers report inner screen damage, possibly from a hinge flaw, as shipping slips to January.
story.title: Some iPhone Duo owners report screens cracking along the hinge
story.why: It is Apple's first foldable, so early durability reports shape how buyers see it.

story.background: A jailbreak removes Apple's software limits so a phone can run unapproved code and tweaks.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: It happened within hours of the phone going on sale.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: AI tools helped build the jailbreak, as with this week's Switch 2 hack.

story.happened: Calif posted the jailbreak on October 23, MacRumors reports. The exploits rely on bugs Calif has disclosed or plans to disclose to Apple. Researcher Stefan Esser said there will be no end-user tool and most bugs should be fixed in iOS 27.2.

meme.take: The iPhone Duo was jailbroken on launch day. Some people really do read the manual first.
meme.top: Apple spent years on the iPhone Duo

story.next: Watch for iOS 27.2 and whether a proof of concept is released.
story.summary: Team Calif showed the foldable running iOS 27.1 with home-screen tweaks on launch day, with help from AI tools.
story.title: Hackers jailbreak the iPhone Duo hours after launch
story.why: A fast jailbreak suggests Apple's newest phone shipped with known flaws, though a public tool is not expected.

story.background: Apple makes the iPhone, the world's best-selling smartphone line. Samsung has sold foldable phones since 2019.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: A foldable iPhone has been rumoured for years.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: At $1,999 it costs more than any iPhone before it.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: Apple reportedly raised orders by about 44% after preorders.

story.happened: Long lines returned to Apple Stores as the Duo launched, MacRumors reports. DigiTimes says Apple raised orders by about 44% to 14 million units over 12 months after strong preorders. Apple has called demand nothing short of extraordinary.

meme.bottom: Finding one is a separate product
meme.take: The iPhone Duo is officially on sale. Actually holding one is still in limited preview.
meme.top: The iPhone Duo is finally on sale

story.next: Watch for when stock catches up with orders and the first sales estimates.
story.summary: Apple's first foldable iPhone went on sale October 23 at $1,999, with walk-in stock scarce and some orders slipping to January.
story.title: Apple's iPhone Duo launches to long lines and thin stock
story.why: It is Apple's first folding phone and its most expensive iPhone yet.

story.background: Ivanti sells IT management and security software. Connect Secure is its VPN gateway for remote workers.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: The flaw is already being exploited.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Ivanti's gateways have been hit by several zero-days in recent years.

story.happened: Ivanti warned on October 13 that a zero-day flaw in Connect Secure is being exploited in attacks, BleepingComputer reports. The company urged customers to install its fix.

meme.take: Plain advice for Connect Secure admins: install Ivanti's fix before anything else.

story.next: Watch for details on who was targeted and whether government agencies order emergency patching.
story.summary: Ivanti urged customers to patch a flaw in its Connect Secure remote access gateway that attackers are already using.
story.title: Ivanti warns a Connect Secure zero-day is being exploited in attacks
story.why: Remote access gateways guard company networks, so exploited flaws there can let attackers in.

story.background: Hardware wallets are small devices that store cryptocurrency keys offline.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: 18,835 unsold devices will be destroyed.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: A stolen verification key could let fake devices pass as genuine.

story.happened: The stolen key is the one Keystone wallets use to check that a device is genuine, The Hacker News reports. Keystone will destroy 18,835 unsold wallets and rotate the key.

meme.take: Keystone lost one key and decided 18,835 locks had to go with it.

story.next: Watch for guidance to existing owners and when new stock ships.
story.summary: Hardware wallet maker Keystone will destroy unsold devices and rotate its key after an attacker obtained the key used for authenticity checks.
story.title: Keystone will destroy 18,835 hardware wallets after its verification key was stolen
story.why: Hardware wallets are meant to be the safest way to hold crypto, so trust in the device is everything.

story.background: SK Hynix and Samsung are the world's largest makers of memory chips used in AI servers.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: AI demand has driven memory chip stocks higher this year.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: It came as AI deals and Anthropic's IPO filing lifted sentiment.

story.happened: SK Hynix gained about 7% and Samsung about 4.8% intraday, the AP reports. In Japan, Advantest rose over 10% and SoftBank about 7%, after Nvidia gained 2.4% in the prior US session.

meme.take: Korean chip stocks jumped again on AI demand. Memory is the one thing AI never forgets to buy.

story.next: Watch for big tech earnings this week and what they say about AI spending.
story.summary: The Kospi rose over 4% in early trading, led by SK Hynix and Samsung, as AI chip stocks rallied across Asia.
story.title: South Korean chip stocks surge as SK Hynix jumps about 7%
story.why: Memory makers are among the biggest winners of AI spending, and their shares move with AI sentiment.

story.background: Ledger is a French company that makes hardware wallets for storing cryptocurrency offline.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Tampered hardware is hard for buyers to detect.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Attackers are targeting the crypto supply chain.

story.happened: Ledger said one affected user's device contained an unauthorized hardware implant, BleepingComputer reports. It linked all reported unexpected drains to devices sold through CryptoBilis, a Malaysia-based reseller it told to stop selling. Ledger called the number affected limited.

meme.bottom: Unless it shipped with a guest
meme.take: Plain lesson from the Ledger case: buy security devices from the maker, not a middleman.

story.next: Watch for how many users were hit and what Ledger offers them.
story.summary: Devices sold through one reseller, CryptoBilis, carried an implant tied to drained crypto wallets, Ledger says.
story.title: Ledger confirms a hardware implant behind crypto thefts from resold wallets
story.why: Hardware wallets are sold as the safest way to hold crypto, so a tampered device undercuts that promise.

story.background: PyPI is the main public library of Python packages, used by millions of developers.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Unpinned installs during the attack window pulled the malicious build.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Attacks on open source packages used by AI developers are rising.

story.happened: LiteLLM suspects a GitHub token leaked in its AI gateway logs let attackers push version 1.107.0, The Hacker News reports. The build carried a credential stealer and a backdoor. The package was quarantined and the Docker images removed.

meme.take: LiteLLM's attackers got in through its logs. Logs remain the most honest employees.

story.next: Watch for LiteLLM's full incident report and advice for users who installed the bad version.
story.summary: LiteLLM says its release pipeline was hijacked on October 21 to push a malicious 1.107.0 build to PyPI and Docker.
story.title: LiteLLM blames a leaked GitHub token for its poisoned release
story.why: LiteLLM sits between many apps and AI models, so a bad release can reach a lot of systems.

story.background: AGENTS.md is a text file developers use to give AI coding agents instructions about a project.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: A single text file was enough to steer the agents.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: It worked on Codex in more than nine of ten attempts.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Attacks aimed at AI agents are rising fast.

story.happened: Forever Security found the file in a Downloads folder, The Hacker News reports. It got OpenAI's Codex to install the package in over 90% of attempts, and a related variant made Claude Code leak OAuth tokens.

meme.take: A text file told coding agents to install malware. They followed instructions beautifully.
meme.top: The agent was told to read the file

story.next: Watch for fixes from OpenAI and Anthropic and new guidance on agent permissions.
story.summary: Researchers found an instruction file that tried to make coding agents install a malicious npm package.
story.title: A malicious AGENTS.md file tricked AI coding agents into installing malware
story.why: Coding agents read files on a computer and act on them, which gives attackers a new way in.

story.background: Samsung is the world's largest maker of memory chips, used in everything from phones to AI servers.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: The shortage could last several more years.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Samsung posted $146.3 billion in quarterly revenue.

story.happened: Instant Gaming reports the warning alongside Samsung's third-quarter revenue of $146.3 billion. Rising memory costs are already being cited in higher device prices, including Apple's new MacBook Pro.

meme.bottom: Prices will remember it for years
meme.take: Memory chips are scarce until 2030, so enjoy your current RAM like a vintage wine.

story.next: Watch for price changes on PCs, consoles and graphics cards heading into 2027.
story.summary: Memory makers warn the shortage pushing up prices could worsen in 2027 and last until 2030, as Samsung posts $146.3 billion in quarterly revenue.
story.title: Memory makers warn the chip shortage could last through 2030
story.why: Memory goes into almost every device, so a long shortage raises prices for PCs, phones and consoles.

story.background: Cambridge Analytica obtained data from about 87 million Facebook profiles through a third-party quiz app.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: $25 billion is described as a record privacy verdict in the US.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Courts have ruled against big tech firms repeatedly over the past year, the NYT reports.

drivers.label: Nostalgia
drivers.text: The case dates back to the 2018 Cambridge Analytica scandal.

story.happened: Judge Francis Mathew set the $25 billion award after a September jury verdict, CBS News reports. Meta had argued it should pay no more than $3.4 billion. Its chief legal officer said the company is confident it will prevail on appeal.

meme.take: Meta offered $3.4 billion. The judge chose a number with more confidence.

story.next: Watch for Meta's appeal, which is expected to tie up the money for some time.
story.summary: A judge set the award after a jury found Facebook misled users about data privacy in a case rooted in Cambridge Analytica.
story.title: Meta is ordered to pay New Mexico a record $25 billion over privacy claims
story.why: It is one of the largest state verdicts in US history and raises the stakes for how platforms describe privacy.

story.background: GitHub is Microsoft's code hosting service, used by most software companies to store and share code.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Meta owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: About 1,500 people are being notified.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Stolen logins remain a top way into company systems.

story.happened: Attackers used stolen employee credentials to access some of Meta's GitHub repositories, SecurityWeek reports. Meta says 99% of what was taken was code, and the rest was personal data on about 1,500 people, mostly US employees, stored there against policy. Notifications began October 13.

meme.take: Meta says 99% of what was taken was just code, which is the good news, somehow.
meme.top: Policy: no personal data in repos

story.next: Watch for what personal data was involved and whether stolen code surfaces online.

stats.label: of stolen data was code, Meta says

story.summary: Attackers used an employee's stolen login to reach some Meta code repositories, the company says.
story.title: Meta says hackers took code and data on about 1,500 people from its GitHub
story.why: A breach at one of the largest tech companies shows how one stolen password can expose source code.

story.background: Meta sells camera-equipped smart glasses made with eyewear company EssilorLuxottica.

drivers.label: Controversy
drivers.text: Hidden cameras in ordinary-looking glasses worry privacy groups.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: The EU's privacy watchdog has also flagged smart glasses risks.

story.happened: Consumentenbond, joined by Offlimits and The Firewall, filed suit at the District Court of Amsterdam, with a hearing set for November 26. They say the glasses make it easy to film people without consent. Meta had said it would keep selling them.

meme.take: Dutch groups sue Meta because its glasses look too much like glasses.

story.next: Watch for the November 26 hearing and any EU regulator action on smart glasses.
story.summary: Consumentenbond and two advocacy groups want Meta to change the glasses and stop processing data unlawfully for AI.
story.title: Dutch consumer groups sue Meta over its camera smart glasses
story.why: The case could set limits in Europe on wearable cameras that look like ordinary glasses.

story.background: Meta sells smart glasses with built-in cameras, microphones and an AI assistant, made with Ray-Ban owner EssilorLuxottica.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Recording without a trigger affects people nearby, not just the wearer.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Meta's glasses are the best-selling smart glasses.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Privacy is the main concern raised about camera glasses.

story.happened: Malwarebytes reports the glasses were found recording conversations without being triggered by the wake phrase. Meta says the issue has been fixed.

meme.take: Meta's glasses recorded without being asked. Meta says they now wait for permission again.
meme.top: The glasses wait for a wake phrase

story.next: Watch for details of how many devices were affected and any regulator interest.
story.summary: Meta's smart glasses were caught recording conversations without the wake phrase, and the company says it has fixed it.
story.title: Meta says it fixed smart glasses that recorded without the wake phrase
story.why: Glasses with cameras and microphones raise privacy worries, and unprompted recording deepens them.

story.background: Cambridge Analytica was a political consultancy that got data on millions of Facebook users, which came to light in 2018.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: A jury found more than 43 million violations of state law.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: $25 billion is a large sum even for Meta.

story.happened: Judge Francis Mathew ordered the $25 billion penalty on October 21 after a September jury verdict, Source NM reports. It is far below the possible maximum of more than $219 billion. Meta plans to appeal.

meme.take: A judge set Meta's penalty at $25 billion, which counts as good news in this line of work.

story.next: Watch for Meta's appeal and whether other states bring similar cases.
story.summary: The penalty covers nearly 44 million violations tied to Cambridge Analytica, and Meta plans to appeal.
story.title: Judge orders Meta to pay $25 billion in New Mexico's privacy case
story.why: It is a very large penalty over user data, even by Big Tech standards.

story.background: Meta owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp and makes most of its money from advertising.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Free cash flow turned negative at about $2.1 billion for the quarter.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Meta's 2026 capital spending outlook tops $135 billion.

story.happened: Revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, with net income of $9.86 billion after a $9.89 billion legal charge. A new filing shows about $825 billion in future commitments, up from about $700 billion in July. The 2026 capex outlook is $135-145 billion.

meme.bottom: And spent slightly more than that
meme.take: Meta grew revenue 26% and spending faster. The classic AI-era business model.

story.next: Watch for whether Meta's 2027 spending plans grow again and how its shares hold up.
story.summary: Meta made $64.6 billion in Q3 but took a $9.9 billion legal charge and raised its yearly spending outlook.
story.title: Meta's revenue jumps 26% while legal costs and AI spending squeeze profit
story.why: Meta is one of the biggest AI spenders, and investors watch whether ads can keep paying for it.

story.background: Pollen Robotics is a French robot maker owned by Hugging Face, the open-source AI platform.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Nvidia's Jensen Huang demonstrated it on stage.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: At $399 it is cheap for a walking robot.

story.happened: Microduck is a 25 cm, 800 g bipedal robot with 15 motors, Martin Cid reports. It costs $399 and passed 20,000 preorders after the GTC Berlin demo. Delivery is targeted before Christmas 2026.

meme.take: Twenty thousand people preordered a walking robot duck. Christmas has a main character.
meme.top: A $399 robot duck learned to walk

story.next: Watch for whether shipping starts on time.
story.summary: The small walking robot drew orders after Jensen Huang showed it off at Nvidia's GTC Berlin, with delivery targeted before Christmas.
story.title: Pollen's $399 Microduck robot passes 20,000 preorders
story.why: Cheap home robots are drawing real buyers, a sign the hobby market may be ready.

story.background: Patch Tuesday is Microsoft's monthly release of security fixes, on the second Tuesday of each month.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: 1,411 fixes is a record for a single Patch Tuesday.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: AI tools are finding software bugs faster than before.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: One flaw is already being used in attacks.

story.happened: Microsoft's October Patch Tuesday fixed 1,411 flaws, 70 of them rated critical, BleepingComputer reports. One zero-day, a Windows Shell flaw that bypasses Mark of the Web, is being exploited. The report links the volume to Microsoft using AI to find bugs.

meme.bottom: Your weekend found a new purpose
meme.take: Microsoft's AI is great at finding bugs. Your reboot schedule is great at absorbing them.

story.next: Watch for details of the exploited flaw and whether huge patch counts become normal.
story.summary: October's update covers 1,411 flaws, including three zero-days, one already being exploited.
story.title: Microsoft fixes a record 1,411 security flaws in one Patch Tuesday
story.why: Almost every Windows user and company has to install these fixes, and the count dwarfs past months.

story.background: Microsoft makes Windows, Office and the Azure cloud, and is a major investor in OpenAI.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Contracted future revenue rose 73% to $677 billion.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Azure grew 48% in the quarter.

story.happened: Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 30% to $63.9 billion and Azure grew 48%. Commercial remaining performance obligation rose 73% to $677 billion. Devices and consumer revenue fell 3%.

meme.bottom: for the tenth quarter in a row
meme.take: Microsoft's results now break records so often that the record is the routine.

story.next: Watch for how investors weigh record spending against the growth.
story.summary: Microsoft's revenue rose 19% to $92.3 billion and net income 32% to $36.6 billion, its tenth record quarter in a row, TechCrunch reports.
story.title: Microsoft posts a 10th straight record quarter with $92.3 billion revenue
story.why: It shows how strongly demand for cloud and AI is flowing into Microsoft's results.

story.background: Microsoft makes Windows, Office and the Azure cloud, and owns Xbox and LinkedIn.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: About 60,000 eligible staff is more than a quarter of the workforce.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Microsoft is spending record sums on AI data centers.

story.happened: About 60,000 staff in the US, Canada, the UK and India are eligible, Reuters reports. Microsoft had about 223,000 full-time employees at the end of June. The offer came days before it reported a record quarter.

meme.take: Microsoft's buyout offer reached a quarter of its staff in the same week as record results.

story.next: Watch for how many staff accept and which teams are most affected.
story.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 eligible staff, more than a quarter of its global workforce.
story.title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees
story.why: It is one of the largest workforce moves by a big tech company this year.

story.background: Navigate360 is an Ohio company that makes school safety and emergency management software.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Navigate360 says it serves more than 35,000 schools.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Exposed data may include Social Security numbers and medical details.

story.happened: An intruder had access from November 2025 to March 2026, the company says. Nevada was first to confirm its SafeVoice tip line was hit and says it cannot notify students because tips are anonymous. The DOJ has opened a criminal investigation.

meme.take: A breach exposed 8.3 million school tip records, and many students cannot even be told.
meme.top: A tip line built to protect students

story.next: Watch for other states confirming impact and the outcome of the federal investigation.
story.summary: A months-long breach exposed crime-tip records that may include students' names and Social Security numbers.
story.title: School safety firm Navigate360 says 8.3 million tip records were stolen
story.why: Anonymous tip lines exist to protect students, so a breach of them is especially serious.

story.background: Nikkei is a Japanese media company that publishes the Nikkei newspaper and owns the Financial Times.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: About 1.83 million records were exposed.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: It is Nikkei's third incident in roughly a month.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Stolen logins are behind many recent breaches.

story.happened: Attackers used stolen credentials to reach a development system on October 7, BleepingComputer reports. About 150,000 of the 1.83 million records held personal details such as names and email addresses. No card data was exposed, and Nikkei says it has seen no misuse.

meme.bottom: Then a second. Now a third
meme.take: Nikkei now publishes breach notices at roughly the pace of a monthly magazine.

story.next: Watch for Nikkei's notices to affected people and any further disclosures.
story.summary: The Japanese media group says stolen credentials exposed about 1.83 million records from a development system.
story.title: Nikkei discloses its third data breach in about a month
story.why: Three breaches in a row at a major news organisation raises questions about its security basics.

story.background: US officials say North Korea uses overseas IT workers with fake identities to earn money for the state.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: About 70 companies across 16 states and DC were affected.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Insiders hired remotely can reach sensitive systems.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: US authorities have pursued similar schemes for several years.

story.happened: The FBI searched more than 40 Texas homes and seized about 187 laptops used to disguise North Korean IT workers as US employees, TechCrunch reports. Two Americans were charged with wire fraud, money laundering and identity theft, and ten China-based people were also charged.

meme.take: Some firms learned their star remote hire was a laptop in Texas run from far away.
meme.top: The remote hire never turned on video

story.next: Watch for more charges and the companies named in court filings.
story.summary: The Justice Department says North Korean workers posed as US staff at about 70 companies in 16 states and DC.
story.title: FBI raids over 40 Texas homes in a North Korean remote IT worker scheme
story.why: Fake remote hires can give hostile states paychecks and access inside ordinary companies.

story.background: The Nvidia App manages drivers and game settings for PCs with Nvidia graphics cards.

drivers.label: Controversy
drivers.text: The feature is on unless users switch it off.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Apps are adding ways for AI agents to control them.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Nvidia's app runs on millions of gaming PCs.

story.happened: Version 11.0.9.565 lets AI agents control the Nvidia App through the MCP protocol by default, Instant Gaming News reports. Agents can tune game graphics, start ShadowPlay recording, check drivers and manage laptop modes. Users can switch it off in Settings.

meme.bottom: It skipped the part where it asks
meme.take: The AI can now adjust your settings, and you can adjust its settings back.
meme.top: Nvidia let AI tune your graphics

story.next: Watch for whether Nvidia changes the default after user feedback.
story.summary: An Nvidia App update lets AI agents adjust game graphics, recording and laptop modes without users opting in.
story.title: Nvidia's app now lets AI agents change your settings by default
story.why: Letting AI agents control software by default is a new step, and some users want to be asked first.

story.background: Neoclouds are companies that rent out Nvidia-powered servers for AI, competing with Amazon, Microsoft and Google.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Nvidia's total exposure is about $171.5 billion, CNBC reports.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: CoreWeave's bond yields have risen above 15%.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Investors are questioning how AI data centers are being financed.

story.happened: CNBC reports Nvidia has $7 billion invested directly in neoclouds and $164.5 billion in guarantees and commitments. CoreWeave's bond yields have topped 15%. Nvidia has agreed to buy up to $6.3 billion of CoreWeave compute if no other buyer is found.

meme.take: Nvidia sells the AI boom its chips and co-signs some of its loans. Supportive, and exposed.
meme.top: Nvidia sold its customers the chips

story.next: Watch for neocloud earnings and any change to Nvidia's financing deals.
story.summary: CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are each down at least 30% this month, putting Nvidia's investments and guarantees in focus.
story.title: Nvidia's $171.5 billion bet on neoclouds faces its first real test
story.why: Nvidia has helped fund its own customers, so their troubles could come back to its books.

story.background: OpenAI is building its own consumer hardware, and has hired former Apple staff.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: OpenAI's device plans put it in direct competition with Apple.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: It is a court fight between two of the most valuable tech companies.

story.happened: Apple's lawsuit alleges OpenAI used confidential Apple information for its hardware project, with more than 100 files said to have been moved. OpenAI agreed not to use the disputed files while the case proceeds, and the suit reached its first major hearing this week.

meme.bottom: OpenAI promises not to peek, for now
meme.take: OpenAI agreed not to open Apple's files, which is the most Apple-like thing it has ever done.

story.next: Watch for the judge's ruling on any preliminary orders.
story.summary: Apple accuses OpenAI of using confidential information for its upcoming hardware, and OpenAI has agreed not to use the disputed files for now.
story.title: Apple's trade secret case against OpenAI reaches its first major hearing
story.why: The case pits two of tech's biggest names against each other as OpenAI moves into devices.

story.background: OpenAI is the company behind ChatGPT and the GPT models. It is based in San Francisco.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: OpenAI makes ChatGPT, one of the most used apps in the world.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: AI labs are seen as prime targets for spying.

drivers.label: Controversy
drivers.text: The FBI director called it a counterintelligence matter.

story.happened: Prosecutors say a chatbot account linked to the engineer's wife asked about building and hiding audio recorders in late September, Fox News reports. OpenAI found the device behind a TV in an executive room on September 30. OpenAI says nothing suggests model weights or customer data were taken.

meme.bottom: Caught with help from a chatbot
meme.take: Prosecutors say the AI helped plan the bug, and OpenAI says AI helped find it. A closed loop.

story.next: Watch for the court case and any findings on what, if anything, was recorded.
story.summary: New details say an account tied to the charged engineer asked about hidden audio recorders days before the device was planted.
story.title: OpenAI recorder case: prosecutors say a linked chatbot account asked how to build bugs
story.why: AI labs guard valuable secrets, and an insider bugging executives would be a serious security breach.

story.background: OpenCode is an open-source AI coding assistant that works with models from several providers.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: API keys can be used to rack up charges.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Attacks on AI developer tools are rising.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Keys for OpenAI and Anthropic models were involved.

story.happened: OpenCode says attackers reached a legacy system it was already shutting down, Cybersecurity News reports. It linked the incident to a large distillation attack and is working with Anthropic, OpenAI and Google. It told affected users to revoke and replace their keys.

meme.bottom: Someone else found a use for it
meme.take: Legacy systems are always about to be shut down. That is when they get the most visitors.
meme.top: OpenCode kept an old system around

story.next: Watch for OpenCode's full account of how attackers got in and how many keys were involved.
story.summary: The AI coding tool says 1.4% of its Console users who linked outside providers may have had their API keys exposed.
story.title: OpenCode says a breach may have exposed users' OpenAI and Anthropic keys
story.why: Stolen AI keys let attackers run up large bills on someone else's account.

story.background: Oppo is a Chinese phone maker and one of the world's largest smartphone brands.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Three 200MP sensors is an unusually high camera count.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: It lands the same week Apple's iPhone Duo goes on sale.

story.happened: Oppo launched the Find X10 and Find X10 Pro Max internationally, Cinco Dias reports. The standard model has two 200MP cameras and the Pro Max three. Both run ColorOS 17 on Android 17, with Spanish prices from about EUR 1,399 and EUR 1,799.

meme.take: Oppo put 600 megapixels on one phone. Lunch has never been documented so thoroughly.

story.next: Watch for camera reviews against Apple's and Samsung's flagships.
story.summary: The Find X10 Pro Max has three 200MP sensors and a 7,150 mAh battery, starting at about EUR 1,799 in Spain.
story.title: Oppo launches the Find X10 phones with up to three 200MP cameras
story.why: Phone makers are racing on camera specs, and this is one of the year's most loaded flagships.

story.background: Oracle is a US software company known for its databases and business applications.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: No login is needed to reach the flaw.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: Probing began days after Oracle released the fix.

story.happened: The flaw needs no login and can be chained to run code on the server. Separately, researchers found that an Oracle PeopleSoft bug exploited since May is really three chained flaws.

meme.take: Oracle patched a critical flaw, and attackers treated the patch notes as a to-do list.

story.next: Watch for CISA warnings and for any breach disclosures tied to the flaw.
story.summary: Attackers are probing an unauthenticated SQL injection flaw in Oracle E-Business Suite that can lead to remote code execution, The Hacker News reports.
story.title: Hackers target a critical Oracle E-Business Suite flaw days after its patch
story.why: E-Business Suite runs finance and supply chains at many large firms, so unpatched systems are prime targets.

story.background: Palantir is a US data analytics company whose software is used by militaries and governments.

drivers.label: Controversy
drivers.text: Europeans fear US tech could be switched off in a crisis.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Palantir is one of the most watched defence tech firms.

story.happened: Louis Mosley, Palantir's executive vice president for the UK and Europe, told Reuters on October 22 there is no remote kill switch for Maven Smart System at NATO's military headquarters. NATO acquired the system in 2025. The claim has not been independently tested.

meme.take: Palantir promised NATO its software cannot be switched off. Normally that is the complaint.
meme.top: Palantir says there is no off switch

story.next: Watch for NATO's own comment and whether European states press for more control of military software.
story.summary: Palantir told Reuters neither it nor the US government can disable the Maven Smart System NATO uses.
story.title: Palantir says it cannot remotely switch off NATO's AI system
story.why: European officials have worried about relying on US tech that Washington might control.

story.background: Counterpoint Research is a market analysis firm that tracks phone and PC sales.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: A 21% fall is one of the steepest quarterly drops in years.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Memory, storage and chip prices have all risen.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Counterpoint expects the decline to deepen to 27% in Q4.

story.happened: Higher prices for RAM, SSDs and processors drove the drop, which ended more than two years of growth, Dataconomy reports. Some PC makers are reviving older DDR4 products to limit price rises. Counterpoint expects 2027 to be broadly flat.

meme.take: PC shipments fell 21% and may fall 27% next. Then, the forecast says, things go flat.

story.next: Watch for PC makers' quarterly results and holiday pricing.

stats.label: Q3 PC shipments, year on year

story.summary: Counterpoint says PC shipments dropped 21% year on year in Q3 and expects a 27% fall in Q4.
story.title: Global PC shipments fall 21% as memory and chip prices climb
story.why: Rising component costs mean higher prices and fewer cheap laptops for buyers this holiday season.

story.background: PHP is a programming language that powers many websites, including those built on WordPress.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Unit 42 counts more than 22.6 million exposed PHP instances.

drivers.label: First of its kind
drivers.text: AI tools were used both to find the bugs and to exploit them.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: One flaw lets attackers run code on a server without logging in.

story.happened: In its October 23 update, Unit 42 said attackers used agentic AI on the two flaws and reached Active Directory at a European government body within two hours. It counts over 22.6 million exposed PHP instances.

meme.take: The PHP bugs were found by AI and exploited by AI. Humans mainly did the patching.
meme.top: AI helped find the PHP bugs

story.next: Watch for patch uptake and further victims being named.
story.summary: BleepingComputer reports the critical PHP flaws are being exploited, after Unit 42 tied AI agents to live attacks.
story.title: PHP2Shell flaws are now being exploited in the wild
story.why: PHP runs a huge share of websites, so active attacks put many servers at risk until they are patched.

story.background: PHP is a programming language that powers many websites, including those built on WordPress.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: The flaws allow takeover without a password.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: About 32.5 million PHP services ran affected versions, per Censys data.

story.happened: Both flaws are rated CVSS 9.2 and allow remote code execution without logging in. PHP patched them on October 21. Dream reported a China-nexus group chaining them with a Linux flaw to root 25 servers in under 15 minutes.

meme.take: PHP2Shell now reaches firewalls, which is like the lock being the easiest way in.
meme.top: Firewalls are meant to keep people out

story.next: Watch for patch guidance from Palo Alto Networks and more CISA warnings.
story.summary: Attackers are exploiting the PHP2Shell flaws in internet-exposed Palo Alto Networks management interfaces, The Hacker News reports.
story.title: PHP2Shell flaws are being used to break into Palo Alto Networks devices
story.why: PHP runs a huge share of the web, and firewalls are prime targets because they guard whole networks.

story.background: Arm licenses chip designs used in most phones. Qualcomm makes Snapdragon processors built on Arm's technology.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: Arm and Qualcomm have fought in court since 2022.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Their chip designs power most smartphones.

drivers.label: Controversy
drivers.text: A win worth two dollars has drawn a lot of attention.

story.happened: A Delaware federal jury found Arm breached its license agreement and acted to disrupt Qualcomm's business, Thurrott reports. Qualcomm was awarded $2 in nominal damages after a five-day trial. Qualcomm had accused Arm of hurting a chip sale to Meta.

meme.take: Qualcomm beat Arm in court and can now afford roughly half a coffee.

story.next: Watch for any appeal by Arm and how the companies' license talks continue.
story.summary: A Delaware jury sided with Qualcomm in its second licensing fight with Arm and awarded nominal damages.
story.title: Jury finds Arm breached Qualcomm's license but awards just $2
story.why: The two companies' chip designs are inside most of the world's phones, so their legal fights matter widely.

story.background: Quest Diagnostics is a major US clinical laboratory company.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Quest handles lab tests for a large share of US patients.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Health data is among the most sensitive kinds of personal information.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: It joins a run of large breaches reported this month.

story.happened: Quest said patient data was accessed and it is still working out how much was taken, TechCrunch reports. Malwarebytes has published guidance for affected patients. The company runs the Quanum system doctors use to order tests.

meme.bottom: On how much data it lost
meme.take: Quest Diagnostics confirmed a breach of patient data and is still working out its size.
meme.top: A lab company is running tests

story.next: Watch for the number of patients affected and notification letters.
story.summary: Attackers compromised Quest's Quanum system for handling test requests and accessed patients' personal and health data.
story.title: Quest Diagnostics confirms patient data was accessed in a breach
story.why: Lab results and health records are among the most sensitive data people have.

story.background: Railway is a cloud platform that developers use to deploy apps and databases.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Stolen keys can open the door to customers' other systems.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Attackers increasingly target the tools developers rely on.

story.happened: Railway disclosed on October 21 that an unauthorised party accessed systems storing customer environment variables and obtained some decrypted contents, including API keys and database credentials. It paused deployments and told users to rotate secrets.

meme.bottom: Customers asked to rotate all keys
meme.take: Railway asks every customer to rotate stored secrets after a breach of its systems.

story.next: Watch for Railway's full incident report and any follow-on attacks using the stolen keys.
story.summary: Railway paused deployments and told users to rotate API keys and database credentials after a breach.
story.title: Cloud platform Railway says attackers obtained customer secrets
story.why: Developers store keys to many other services on platforms like Railway, so one breach can spread.

story.background: Ransomware is malware that locks or steals data and demands payment to release it.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Ransomware can shut down hospitals, factories and offices.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Both attackers and defenders are adopting AI tools.

story.happened: 84% of organizations hit by ransomware said attackers used AI somewhere in the attack, a Semperis survey found, CBS News reports. 44% said criminals exploited the victims' own AI systems. Many breaches still relied on familiar identity and security weaknesses.

meme.bottom: So did the people attacking them
meme.take: Ransomware gangs have adopted AI faster than most procurement departments.

story.next: Watch for whether companies change how they secure their own AI tools.
story.summary: A Semperis survey found 84% of organizations hit by ransomware said attackers used AI somewhere in the attack.
story.title: Survey finds attackers used AI in most ransomware attacks
story.why: AI may be making common cyberattacks faster and cheaper to run.

story.background: Salesforce is a leading maker of business software for sales and marketing. Braze helps brands message customers.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: The deal is worth nearly $5.7 billion.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Braze shares jumped about 50% in a day.

story.happened: Salesforce will pay $47.50 per share in cash for Braze, nearly $5.7 billion in enterprise value, Bloomberg reports. The deal is expected to close from February 2027. Braze shares rose about 50% on the news.

meme.take: Salesforce's stock fell 2% on the news, the traditional fee for writing a $5.7 billion check.

story.next: Watch for regulatory review and how Salesforce fits Braze into its marketing products.
story.summary: The all-cash deal pays $47.50 a share, sending Braze stock up about 50% while Salesforce fell about 2%.
story.title: Salesforce agrees to buy marketing platform Braze for about $5.7 billion
story.why: It is one of the year's larger software deals, as Salesforce pushes deeper into customer marketing.

story.background: Samsung is South Korea's largest company and one of the few firms making leading-edge chips.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: A 2.7 million square foot plant is a huge investment.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: It counters TSMC's expansion in Arizona.

story.happened: SammyFans, citing DigiTimes, reports Samsung will break ground on a second Taylor, Texas fab in November. The expansion covers 2.7 million square feet, with mass production planned for 2030. Fab 1 aims to start by the end of 2026.

meme.bottom: So naturally it is building another
meme.take: Samsung starts a second Texas chip plant before the first opens, like ordering dessert early.
meme.top: Samsung's first Texas fab isn't open

story.next: Watch for Samsung confirming the groundbreaking and its first customers.
story.summary: Samsung plans to break ground on Taylor Fab 2 in November, DigiTimes reports, while Fab 1 prepares to begin operating.
story.title: Samsung is reported to start a second Texas chip fab before its first opens
story.why: It is a sign of how much chipmakers expect AI demand to grow in the US.

story.background: HBM is stacked high-speed memory used alongside AI processors such as Nvidia's GPUs.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: Samsung and TSMC compete head to head in chipmaking.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: HBM demand is forecast to nearly double next year.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Nvidia is the leading maker of AI chips.

story.happened: Seoul Economic Daily reports Nvidia is co-designing the base die with both firms. TSMC's 3nm yield is estimated above 90%, against about 60% for Samsung's 2nm. UBS projects HBM demand up 91% next year, ahead of supply.

meme.bottom: So it called its biggest rival
meme.take: AI memory demand is so high that Samsung and TSMC are briefly on the same side.

story.next: Watch for confirmation from Samsung, TSMC or Nvidia.
story.summary: Samsung will reportedly tap TSMC's 3nm process for the base die of Nvidia's custom HBM, its first such handoff.
story.title: Samsung is reported to use rival TSMC to make base dies for Nvidia's custom memory
story.why: It shows how tight AI memory supply is, pushing even fierce rivals to work together.

story.background: Fire TV is Amazon's streaming platform, and Google TV runs on Google's Android TV system.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: Ad-free TVs are a long-running wish for many viewers.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: AI coding tools let non-experts take on technical projects.

drivers.label: Controversy
drivers.text: TV makers rely on ads and data for revenue.

story.happened: TechCrunch reports two GitHub projects for stripping smart TVs. One, cleanyourtv, used Claude Code to find a TV on the network, remove 25 Xiaomi packages and write a new launcher. Another, dumbtv, was built with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Claude models.

meme.bottom: So the owner asked an AI to fix it
meme.take: Smart TVs spent years getting smarter. Their owners just asked for them to be quieter.

story.next: Watch for how Amazon and Google respond to modified devices.
story.summary: Developers are using Claude Code and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash to remove ads and tracking from Fire TV and Google TV devices.
story.title: People are using AI coding tools to strip ads from their smart TVs
story.why: Many people dislike the ads and data collection on smart TVs, and AI tools make modding them easier.

story.background: SpaceX makes rockets and runs Starlink. It went public in June and now includes xAI and Cursor.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Q4 spending guidance is roughly double Q3's $19.6 billion.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Elon Musk runs both SpaceX and Tesla.

story.happened: Net income was $4.4 billion, though about $1.6 billion came from below the operating line. SpaceX guided fourth-quarter capital spending to $35-40 billion. Elon Musk said SpaceX and Tesla have formed committees to discuss a possible merger.

meme.take: SpaceX turned a profit, then planned to nearly double spending. Rocket science, for budgets.

story.next: Watch for any merger terms between SpaceX and Tesla and whether spending keeps climbing.
story.summary: SpaceX's third-quarter revenue rose 161% to $14.6 billion, with its AI unit now bringing in about half.
story.title: SpaceX posts a $4.4 billion profit and plans to nearly double spending
story.why: SpaceX is one of the most valuable public companies and a major AI spender since absorbing xAI.

story.background: Tailscale makes networking software that connects devices into a private network over the internet.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: One compromised device could reach root-only services elsewhere.

drivers.label: Controversy
drivers.text: The research was published before a patch was ready.

story.happened: Erica Windisch of Cyberdione Labs published the flaws before a fix and showed the attack in a lab. Tailscale has now shipped patches, The Hacker News reports.

meme.take: Tailscale shipped its fix, ending a brief spell when the bug had better press than the patch.

story.next: Watch for users updating their Tailscale clients and any further findings.
story.summary: Tailscale fixed SSH forwarding flaws that could let an attacker on a trusted device reach root-only services on other servers.
story.title: Tailscale patches the Tailworm SSH flaws
story.why: Tailscale is used to link company devices securely, so flaws in it can open doors across a network.

story.background: Taiwan is home to TSMC, which manufactures most of the world's most advanced chips.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: AI chips are at the centre of US-China tensions.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Smuggling has been a gap in existing export controls.

story.happened: Economic Affairs Minister Kung Ming-hsin plans to add AI servers and advanced chips to Taiwan's controlled commodities, Startup Fortune reports. Unauthorized shipments to Chinese buyers would be a crime under the Foreign Trade Act.

meme.bottom: Now it is checking the luggage
meme.take: Taiwan will criminalize AI chip smuggling, so the servers will have to declare themselves.
meme.top: Taiwan makes the world's best chips

story.next: Watch for the formal rule change and how it is enforced.
story.summary: Taiwan plans to list AI servers and advanced chips as controlled goods, making unauthorized shipments to Chinese buyers a criminal offence.
story.title: Taiwan moves to make smuggling AI chips to China a crime
story.why: Taiwan makes most of the world's advanced chips, so its export rules matter for the US-China tech contest.

story.background: Taiwan is home to TSMC, which makes most of the world's advanced chips, including Nvidia's.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Each site is budgeted at $2 billion to $4 billion.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Chip suppliers are expanding into the US.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: The park is built around Nvidia's supply chain.

story.happened: Taiwan's economy minister Kung Ming-hsin announced funding for US industrial parks for smaller suppliers to Nvidia, TSMC and Foxconn, Bloomberg reports. The first, in Texas, could cost up to $4 billion, and Taiwan has secured the land.

meme.take: Taiwan is building a whole town in Texas so Nvidia's suppliers can be closer to its money.

story.next: Watch for which suppliers sign up and when construction begins.
story.summary: Taiwan plans US industrial parks for the smaller firms that supply Nvidia, TSMC and Foxconn, starting in Texas.
story.title: Taiwan to fund a Texas industrial park of up to $4 billion for Nvidia's suppliers
story.why: It shows the chip supply chain moving into the US as demand for AI hardware grows.

story.background: Full Self-Driving is Tesla's paid driver-assistance software, which still needs an attentive driver.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Tesla's self-driving promises are among tech's most debated.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: A class action could have covered many FSD buyers.

story.happened: A three-judge Ninth Circuit panel on October 16 reversed certification of two damages classes and one injunctive class in LoSavio v. Tesla, Bloomberg Law reports. Individual claims stay before Judge Rita Lin.

meme.bottom: Now has to find its own way
meme.take: Tesla buyers lost their class action, so each must now navigate the courts manually.

story.next: Watch for whether plaintiffs seek a rehearing or refile on a narrower basis.
story.summary: The Ninth Circuit reversed class status in a suit claiming Tesla misled buyers about Full Self-Driving, though individual claims continue.
story.title: Appeals court decertifies class action over Tesla's self-driving claims
story.why: Class status lets thousands of buyers sue together, so losing it greatly changes the case.

story.background: Tesla is the electric car maker led by Elon Musk. It also sells energy storage and is building humanoid robots.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Elon Musk's companies draw coverage far beyond the car industry.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: R&D spending rose 69% to $2.76 billion as AI work grows.

story.happened: Net income fell 44% to $787 million on roughly flat revenue of $28.05 billion, AP reports. Operating income dropped 56% to $718 million while R&D rose 69%, Electrek reports. Free cash flow was about $1.5 billion.

meme.take: Tesla made less money than last year and more than expected. Both are true.

story.next: Watch for updates on Optimus robot production and the robotaxi rollout.
story.summary: Tesla's Q3 net income fell to $787 million, but adjusted EPS of $0.48 beat estimates.
story.title: Tesla's profit falls 44% even as it beats forecasts
story.why: Investors are weighing Tesla's falling car profits against its bets on robots and robotaxis.

story.background: TikTok is a short-video app owned by ByteDance. TikTok Live lets users stream and receive gifts.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Child safety is the most serious charge a social platform can face.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: TikTok has a huge young audience.

story.happened: Depositions from TikTok staff, reported by NPR, say executives ignored internal warnings about child sexual exploitation on TikTok Live. Staff said minors appeared in livestreams. The claims come from testimony in legal proceedings.

meme.take: Testimony says the warnings about TikTok Live were raised internally and not acted on.

story.next: Watch for TikTok's response and whether the testimony is used in court.
story.summary: NPR reports staff told executives that minors were appearing in livestreams where exploitation took place.
story.title: Depositions say TikTok executives ignored warnings about child exploitation on Live
story.why: It adds to legal and political pressure on TikTok over how it protects young users.

story.background: TSMC is a Taiwanese company that manufactures chips designed by other firms.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: TSMC makes chips for Nvidia, Apple and AMD.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Net profit margin reached 51.1%.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: It reported in the middle of a chip stock selloff.

story.happened: TSMC's third-quarter revenue rose 50.9% from a year earlier to $46.72 billion, and net income rose 68.7%, the company said on October 15. Chips at 7nm and below made up 79% of wafer revenue. It guided fourth-quarter revenue to $52.3 to $54.3 billion.

meme.take: TSMC posted a record quarter. Markets will now find a way to be worried about it.

story.next: Watch for whether the strong guidance steadies chip stocks after this week's selloff.

stats.label: net income growth, year on year

story.summary: The world's biggest chipmaker earned $46.7 billion in third-quarter revenue and guided higher for the fourth.
story.title: TSMC posts record quarter as AI chip demand lifts profit 69%
story.why: TSMC makes most advanced AI chips, so its results are a direct read on AI demand.

story.background: UEFI is the firmware that starts a computer before the operating system loads. EDK II is its open-source reference code.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Code that runs before boot is very hard to detect.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: EDK II is widely used open-source firmware code.

story.happened: The bug affects servers that boot over the network and has existed for about 16 years. Because it runs before Secure Boot checks, normal security tools may not see it.

meme.bottom: It has outlasted most of the servers
meme.take: A UEFI flaw turned 16 before anyone noticed it was in the room.

story.next: Watch for firmware updates from server and motherboard makers.
story.summary: A long-standing flaw in EDK II firmware lets an attacker on the adjacent network run code during network boot, The Hacker News reports.
story.title: A 16-year-old UEFI flaw lets attackers run code before Secure Boot
story.why: Code that runs before Secure Boot can sit below the operating system's defences.

story.background: UNM Health runs New Mexico's main academic hospital in Albuquerque.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: The incident disrupted hospital care.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Health systems are frequent targets of cyberattacks.

story.happened: UNM Health urged people to avoid its main hospital and cancelled appointments at more than 30 clinics, SecurityWeek reports. The health system described the problem as a cybersecurity issue.

meme.take: A cyber incident disrupted care at UNM Health. Patients are being sent elsewhere.
meme.top: A New Mexico hospital diverts patients

story.next: Watch for when services are restored and what caused the incident.
story.summary: University of New Mexico Health told people not to come to its main Albuquerque hospital and cancelled appointments at over 30 clinics.
story.title: A cyber incident forces New Mexico's largest health system to divert patients
story.why: Cyber incidents at hospitals can directly disrupt patient care.

story.background: MiraclePlus is a Beijing startup accelerator founded by former Y Combinator China head Lu Qi.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: AI is at the centre of US-China tech competition.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: The case involves Google's AI technology.

story.happened: The US sanctioned MiraclePlus for financing Zhisuan, founded by Ding Linwei, who was convicted this year of stealing Google AI trade secrets, Bloomberg reports. The State Department action covers five Chinese entities.

meme.take: MiraclePlus backed a founder with a remarkable head start. Washington asked where from.
meme.top: A startup ran on Google's secrets

story.next: Watch for China's response and whether more investors are added to the list.
story.summary: MiraclePlus, often called China's Y Combinator, funded a startup founded by a man convicted of stealing Google's AI trade secrets.
story.title: US blacklists Chinese investor MiraclePlus over a Google AI secrets case
story.why: It shows Washington widening its fight over AI technology from chips to the investors behind startups.

story.background: Verizon is the largest wireless carrier in the US by subscribers.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: A $10 monthly fee adds $120 a year.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: It arrives alongside the iPhone Duo launch.

story.happened: MacRumors reports the feature lets one phone number move between two iPhones, with only one active at a time. Verizon says it is coming soon and will work with the iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro.

meme.take: Verizon will move your number between two iPhones for $10 a month. Leaving costs less.

story.next: Watch for whether AT&T and T-Mobile charge for the feature too.
story.summary: Verizon plans a monthly fee for iOS 27's feature that lets one number switch between a main and companion iPhone.
story.title: Verizon will charge $10 a month to share one number across two iPhones
story.why: Carrier fees on new phone features tend to annoy customers, especially on a $1,999 phone.

story.background: Volvo Cars is a Swedish carmaker majority-owned by China's Geely.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: It swung from a SEK 6.4 billion profit to a SEK 5.6 billion loss.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: Western carmakers face fierce competition from local brands in China.

story.happened: Volvo Cars reported a SEK 5.6 billion operating loss, against a SEK 6.4 billion profit a year earlier, and announced 2,500 job cuts, TheStreet reports. Its shares fell 24% on the day.

meme.bottom: Its share price had no airbag
meme.take: Volvo builds some of the safest cars on the road. Its stock had no such protection on Friday.

story.next: Watch for where the cuts fall and any change to its electric car plans.
story.summary: The carmaker swung to a third-quarter operating loss of SEK 5.6 billion, hit by weak sales in China.
story.title: Volvo Cars shares drop 24% as it cuts 2,500 jobs
story.why: It is a sharp sign of how tough China's car market has become for Western brands.

story.background: Wayve is a British self-driving startup. Stellantis owns brands including Fiat, Jeep, Peugeot and Maserati.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Nvidia, Stellantis and the French government are all involved.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: Integration into two cars took under four weeks, the partners say.

story.happened: The deal was announced in Paris on October 23, Unite.ai reports. Wayve's software was fitted to a Fiat 500e and a Maserati Grecale in under four weeks. The supervised system is due in 2028.

meme.bottom: Only one of them got the ego
meme.take: Wayve fitted its driving AI to a Fiat and a Maserati. Software is not a snob.
meme.top: A Fiat and a Maserati share a brain

story.next: Watch for which Stellantis models get the system first.
story.summary: The partners plan a supervised hands-free driving system for 2028, starting in North America.
story.title: Wayve, Stellantis and Nvidia team up with France on hands-free driving
story.why: Self-driving tech is moving from robotaxi trials into mass-market cars.

story.background: Bug bounties pay researchers who report security flaws privately so companies can fix them first.

drivers.label: First of its kind
drivers.text: A full-chain browser exploit built largely by AI agents is new.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: The bounty paid out $250,000 for about $40,000 of compute.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: The same skills could help attackers as well as defenders.

story.happened: XBOW says its AI agents built a full-chain Chrome exploit from three bugs, earning Google's $250,000 bounty, CyberInsider reports. The work took six days and about $40,000 of compute, with humans choosing targets. Google has patched all three flaws.

meme.take: The AI found three Chrome bugs and a business model.

story.next: Watch for how browser makers and bug bounty programs adjust to AI-found exploits.
story.summary: Security firm XBOW says agents running OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol chained three bugs in six days for about $40,000 in compute.
story.title: AI agents built a full Chrome exploit that earned a $250,000 Google bounty
story.why: It shows AI can now do serious offensive security work that used to take expert teams.

story.background: Android XR is Google's operating system for headsets and smart glasses.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Tech companies are racing to put AI assistants into glasses.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Google's Gemini is built in.

story.happened: The glasses weigh under 95 grams and connect to a separate processing unit, Google says. US shipments are expected in mid-November.

meme.take: XREAL's glasses put an assistant in your eyeline, for people who found phones too far away.
meme.top: Gemini now lives on your face

story.next: Watch for reviews when US shipments begin in mid-November.
story.summary: XREAL's AURA glasses run Android XR with Gemini, a 70-degree field of view and a tethered processing unit, starting at $1,099.
story.title: XREAL opens orders for Android XR glasses with built-in Gemini
story.why: They are an early test of whether people will wear AI assistants on their faces.

story.background: Yandex is Russia's largest internet company, running search, taxis, maps and cloud services.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: More than 80 Yandex Cloud services were disrupted, Kyiv Post says.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Yandex has added drone attacks to its force majeure terms.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: Three sites were hit within four days.

story.happened: Drone attacks damaged three Yandex data centers, forcing two to shut and one to be partly disabled, BleepingComputer reports. Yandex confirmed outages as users lost access to cloud files. Yandex Go taxi ordering also failed across Russia.

meme.take: A sober reminder that war now reaches the cloud and the apps people rely on.

story.next: Watch for how quickly Yandex restores services and whether more sites are hit.

stats.label: data centers hit in four days

story.summary: Russian taxi, cloud and smart home services went down after the Vladimir site closed on October 11.
story.title: Drone strikes shut a third Yandex data center in four days
story.why: Data centers have become wartime targets, with direct effects on everyday apps.
